name: Sound-trap microplastic breaker
subtitle: ultrasound holds plastic specks while light destroys them

effects.effect: a strong sound wave pushes steadily on small objects
energetic light breaks molecules into pieces

effect: a strong sound wave pushes steadily on small objects
how: Treated sewage still sends billions of plastic specks into rivers, too small for any screen to catch. As the water flows through a channel, standing ultrasound waves push the specks into thin sheets where the sound is quietest (acoustic radiation pressure), and strong ultraviolet light aimed at just those sheets snaps the plastic's chemical bonds (photodissociation) until it breaks down.
obstacle: Ultraviolet breaks plastic slowly, and half-broken plastic makes even smaller specks, so the trap must hold them for a long time.
why: Microplastics slip through every treatment plant; destroying them at the outfall stops them at the source.
real: Acoustic standing-wave trapping of microplastics is built (HKRITA Acousweep, EchoGrid) and UV photodegradation is studied separately, but nothing combines acoustic trapping with targeted UV breakdown.
